title: Founding of modern Singapore
examples: What was important about Singapore in 1819?
Why did the British establish Singapore?
What does 'free port' mean for a trading town?

explain.say: In 1819, the British arrived in Singapore. They wanted to establish a trading post here.
The location of Singapore was very strategic for trade. It was near major sea routes.
The British declared Singapore a free port. This meant low taxes on goods.

draw.text: Free port: low taxes on goods

explain.say: This status attracted many merchants from all over the world. They wanted to trade easily.
In everyday life, a free port helps a town grow fast. Think about a local market.
A common mistake is thinking the British arrived alone. Many local people were already trading there.

faq.q: Why did the British establish Singapore?
faq.a: The British wanted a strategic trading post. This allowed them to control important sea routes in the region.
asks: What was the main reason for the British presence?
Why was this location important for trade?

faq.q: What does 'free port' mean for a trading town?
faq.a: It means that goods can be traded with very few taxes or duties. This makes the place very attractive to merchants.
asks: What benefits does a free port offer?

faq.q: Was Singapore always a major trading hub?
faq.a: No, while it became one, trade activity was already present before the British arrival in 1819.
asks: Did trade start with the British?
What was the trade situation before 1819?

faq.q: How did the 1819 arrival change Singapore?
faq.a: It formalized and greatly expanded Singapore's role in global trade. The British structure helped it grow rapidly.
asks: What was the impact of the British arrival?
Did the British just move things in?

faq.q: Was the location important for military reasons too?
faq.a: Yes, controlling the sea routes was vital for both trade and military power in the region.
asks: Did the British control the area by force?

facts: The British established a presence in Singapore in 1819.
Its location on key sea routes made it valuable for trade.
Declaring it a free port encouraged international trade.
This status attracted merchants from many different countries.

quiz.say: The primary reason the British established Singapore was to:
quiz.why: This location was key for controlling the flow of goods and power in the region.

wrong.0: While military control was a factor, the main draw was economic trade.
wrong.1: The primary focus was on commerce, not just population movement.
wrong.2: The trade potential was more important than any single resource discovered.

quiz.say: What did the 'free port' status mainly provide to traders?
quiz.why: Low taxes made trading goods in Singapore much cheaper and more appealing.

wrong.0: Safety was important, but the tax benefit was the main economic incentive.
wrong.1: The 'free' part meant it was open to many nations, not just Britain.
wrong.2: While the British governed, the free port status focused on economic freedom.

quiz.say: If a town has low taxes on goods, it is likely to:
quiz.show: See an increase in trade volume

options.show: See an increase in trade volume
options.say: See an increase in trade volume

options.show: Become less diverse in its population
options.say: Become less diverse in its population

quiz.why: Fewer taxes mean goods are cheaper, which encourages more people to trade.

wrong.1: Economic success usually attracts people from many different places.
wrong.2: The concept of a free port implies wide, global trade connections.
wrong.3: Successful trade leads to continuous investment and growth.
